localFacts.fact: El Debate (jurist Carlos Mateos Rodrigo, 2025): owning a ballesta is regulated by the Reglamento de Armas (categoría 7ª.2, licencia tipo E); hunting with it is regulated by each comunidad autónoma: Extremadura, Aragón and the Comunidad Valenciana allow it, Castilla-La Mancha, La Rioja and the País Vasco ban it expressly, and most regions do not mention it. Check your community's orden de vedas.
The EU Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC) lists crossbows in Annex VI among prohibited means of capture and killing.
In Spain the Primos Trigger Stick Gen3 is sold as a 'trípode de caza', adjustable from 61 to 157 cm.
Foto Erhardt lists the Vanguard Quest T62U at 1020 g, 157,5 cm max. height and 70 cm pack size.

localPainPoints.pain: Spanish hunters are unsure whether crossbow hunting is allowed in their region.
localPainPoints.fix: Check the orden de vedas of your comunidad autónoma before the season; the tripod also works for tiro and sighting in.

quotes.text: La ballesta está prohibida en la mayor parte de comunidades autónomas y en las restantes se irá prohibiendo.

localPainPoints.pain: Hunters with a bad shoulder look at the crossbow because they cannot draw or hold a bow.
localPainPoints.fix: A clamp tripod (BOG DeathGrip) carries the weight so you do not hold the crossbow up; Crossbow Magazine's youth-hunter point from the English post.

quotes.text: como estoy jodido con el hombro como sabes, pues por algún momento se me ha pasado por la cabeza la ballesta

localGain.point: Explains that crossbow hunting rules depend on the comunidad autónoma, with the regions El Debate names.
Answers the shoulder-injury reader with the hands-free clamp pick.
